andhraPradesh.headline: Foundation laid for ₹1 lakh-crore Global Horticulture Hub across 10 Andhra Pradesh districts
facts: The foundation stone for the Global Horticulture Hub–Rayalaseema Rising was laid at Madanapalle in Annamayya district on 2 October.
The three-phase plan has an estimated outlay of ₹1 lakh crore: ₹40,352 crore in government investment and about ₹60,000 crore expected from private investment.
It covers 10 districts through 201 clusters across 303 mandals and 5,869 villages.
The plan seeks to expand horticulture area from 8.41 lakh hectares to 14.41 lakh hectares; this is a target, not completed expansion.
The listed districts are Anantapur, Annamayya, Chittoor, Kurnool, Nandyal, Sri Sathya Sai, Tirupati, Kadapa, Prakasam and Markapuram.
andhraPradesh.summary: The project moved from planning to the foundation-stone stage at Madanapalle on 2 October. Its stated approach links horticulture expansion with irrigation, rural roads, processing and export infrastructure; the private-sector component remains expected investment, not expenditure already made.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Dryland agriculture, horticulture-led rural development, irrigation and agricultural value chains.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the project’s name, Madanapalle location, 10-district coverage and planned public/private financing split.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess whether integrated irrigation, farm-to-market infrastructure and private processing can improve climate resilience and farmer incomes in drought-prone Rayalaseema.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The project is located in Annamayya district and covers 10 Andhra Pradesh districts, including Rayalaseema and Markapuram.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh High Court sets aside enhanced BC quota orders for local-body polls
facts: On 1 October, a Division Bench of the Andhra Pradesh High Court set aside G.O.Ms.No.105, dated 20 August 2026, providing 34% BC reservation in panchayat institutions, and G.O.Rt.No.1065, dated 19 August 2026, providing 33.33% in urban local bodies.
The Court held that the orders exceeded the 50% aggregate ceiling for SC, ST and BC vertical reservations without the required empirical exercise.
It left open the possibility of reconsidering BC reservation beyond 50% after the state undertakes the required empirical exercise.
The Court directed the State and State Election Commission to begin the local-body election process expeditiously, preferably within six weeks.
andhraPradesh.summary: The High Court invalidated the state orders enhancing BC reservation in rural and urban local bodies, applying the Supreme Court’s reservation-ceiling and empirical-data principles. It also called for the local-body election process to begin promptly, while leaving room for the state to revisit the quota after the required evidence-gathering exercise.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Constitutional reservations, local self-government, judicial review and the 50% reservation ceiling.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Distinguish the orders: 34% BC quota for panchayat institutions and 33.33% for urban local bodies were set aside; the Court cited the 50% aggregate ceiling and required empirical exercise.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine the balance between evidence-based reservation policy for local bodies, backward-class representation and timely elections under constitutional local governance.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The judgment concerns Andhra Pradesh government orders and elections to the state’s gram panchayats and urban local bodies.

sources.title: Thandava Yogesh v. The State Election Commission and others
sources.publisher: Andhra Pradesh High Court judgment text via Indian Kanoon

sources.publisher: The New Indian Express

- **Decision:** Set aside **G.O.Ms.No.105**, dated **20 August 2026**, providing **34%** BC reservation in panchayat institutions, and **G.O.Rt.No.1065**, dated **19 August 2026**, providing **33.33%** in urban local bodies

# 2. Reason and directions
- **Reservation ceiling:** Orders exceeded the **50%** aggregate ceiling for **SC**, **ST** and **BC** vertical reservations without the required empirical exercise
- **Scope for reconsideration:** BC reservation beyond **50%** may be reconsidered after the State undertakes the required empirical exercise
- **Election process:** Directed the **State** and **State Election Commission** to begin local-body elections expeditiously, preferably within **six weeks**
- ⚠ **Trap:** The Court set aside the specified orders; it left open reconsideration of reservation beyond **50%** after the required empirical exercise
> Exam angle: Identify the High Court ruling’s two government orders, reservation percentages, **50%** ceiling and election-process direction.

andhraPradesh.headline: Reliance announces a proposed ₹1 lakh-crore compressed-biogas investment plan for Andhra Pradesh
facts: Reliance Industries Executive Director Anant M. Ambani announced a plan to invest ₹1 lakh crore in compressed biogas (CBG) plants in Andhra Pradesh.
The announcement was made at the Madanapalle event on 2 October; the reported plan is not evidence that the investment has been spent or that plants are operational.
Ambani projected more than 3 lakh jobs and nearly ₹60,000 crore in state revenue over coming decades; these are projections, not realised outcomes.
CBG plants can convert organic feedstocks, including agricultural residues, into fuel; no district-wise locations or construction schedule were specified in the cited announcement.
andhraPradesh.summary: Reliance announced a proposed state-wide CBG investment plan during the Madanapalle event. The company’s stated investment, jobs and revenue figures are forward-looking claims; the announcement did not establish project-wise approvals, locations or construction progress.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Compressed biogas, bioenergy, circular economy and private investment in renewable fuels.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: CBG is compressed biogas produced from organic material; treat the ₹1 lakh-crore amount and employment figure as an announced plan and projection, not completed investment or existing jobs.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how agricultural-waste-to-energy projects may diversify rural incomes and support energy transition, while identifying land, feedstock, water and implementation safeguards.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The announced CBG programme is for Andhra Pradesh; it was announced at Madanapalle, Annamayya district, but district-wise plant locations were not specified.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh and Reliance sign MoU for Indian School of Agriculture at Madanapalle
facts: The Andhra Pradesh government and Reliance Industries signed an MoU for establishing and managing the proposed Indian School of Agriculture (ISA).
The foundation-stone plaque for the ISA was unveiled at Madanapalle in Annamayya district on 2 October.
The school is described as being planned on the lines of the Indian School of Business and focused on agriculture; operational details and an opening date were not stated in the cited report.

andhraPradesh.summary: The MoU and foundation-stone event mark a proposed agriculture-education and research partnership in Madanapalle. The school is not yet reported as operational, and the cited announcement did not provide a commissioning date or detailed programme structure.

andhraPradesh.headline: Twelve Andhra Pradesh government hospitals and health centres receive Swachh Andhra awards
facts: Twelve Andhra Pradesh government hospitals and health centres received Swachh Andhra State-Level Awards 2026 under the Swarna Andhra–Swachh Andhra initiative.
The award assessment used criteria including separate toilets, handwashing facilities, toilet cleanliness, infection-control inspections and cleanliness guidance or displays.
Recipients named in the report included Atmakur District Hospital in Nellore, Pendurthy Community Health Centre and facilities in Krishna, NTR, Kurnool, Markapuram and Tirupati districts.
The award ceremony was held in Vijayawada on 2 October; district-level awards were also to be presented by respective collectors.
andhraPradesh.summary: The state recognised 12 public hospitals and health centres for sanitation and cleanliness measures under its Swachh Andhra initiative. The assessment criteria linked facility hygiene with handwashing and infection-control practices; the award announcement itself does not establish subsequent health-outcome improvements.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Public-health infrastructure, sanitation, infection prevention and local governance.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Know the award initiative and its hospital-assessment elements: toilets, handwashing, cleanliness and infection control.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how measurable cleanliness standards and third-party inspections can strengthen public-health facility governance, alongside routine monitoring and patient-safety outcomes.

national.headline: Government extends RoDTEP scheme through 31 December 2026
facts: The Department of Commerce extended the Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) scheme through 31 December 2026.
The extension was issued under Notification No. 41/2026-27 dated 30 September 2026.
The scheme refunds embedded, un-rebated Central, State and local duties, taxes and levies borne on exported products.
Existing rates and value caps remained unchanged during the extension.
Eligible exporters include Domestic Tariff Area units, Advance Authorisation holders, Special Economic Zone units and Export Oriented Units.
national.summary: The Union Government continued RoDTEP support for eligible exporters until 31 December 2026. The extension preserves existing rates and caps, supporting export competitiveness while the scheme remains in force.
national.staticLink: Export promotion, remission of embedded taxes and India’s balance of trade.
national.prelimsTakeaway: RoDTEP stands for Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products; the extension runs through 31 December 2026.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how remission of embedded taxes can support export competitiveness and discuss the balance between export incentives and fiscal discipline.

- **What:** The **Department of Commerce** extended the **Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP)** scheme through **31 December 2026**.
- **Status:** **ONGOING**; extension issued under **Notification No. 41/2026-27**, dated **30 September 2026**.

# 2. Scheme details
- **Objective:** Refund of embedded, un-rebated **Central, State and local duties, taxes and levies** borne on exported products; support for export competitiveness.
- **Rates and caps:** Existing rates and value caps remained **unchanged**.
- **Eligible exporters:**
| Category | Eligible units |
|---|---|
| Exporter types | **Domestic Tariff Area units**; **Advance Authorisation holders**; **Special Economic Zone units**; **Export Oriented Units** |
- ⚠ **Trap:** Extension of the scheme did **not** revise its existing rates or value caps.

# 3. Exam focus
> Exam angle: **Scheme / Yojana**—test RoDTEP’s full form, purpose, extension date and eligible exporters.

national.headline: RELIEF exporter-support timelines extended amid West Asia logistics disruption
facts: The Department of Commerce extended timelines under Component II of RELIEF through Notification No. 37/2026-27 dated 30 September 2026.
RELIEF means Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation and is a time-bound intervention under the Export Promotion Mission.
Component II encourages exporters to obtain ECGC cover for eligible upcoming shipments to specified regions, with 95% risk coverage.
Eligible cargo includes full-container-load, less-than-container-load and reefer containers; energy shipments are excluded.
RELIEF was launched on 19 March 2026 to support exporters affected by freight, insurance and war-related risks associated with West Asia maritime disruptions.
national.summary: The Government extended Component II timelines under RELIEF in response to continuing West Asia-related maritime logistics disruption. The intervention offers eligible exporters ECGC-backed risk coverage and limits premium increases for the eligible period.
national.staticLink: Export risk insurance, trade facilitation and resilience of supply chains.
national.prelimsTakeaway: RELIEF expands to Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation; Component II provides 95% risk coverage through ECGC for specified eligible shipments.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how targeted export-risk support can protect trade flows during geopolitical and logistics shocks, while considering its coverage and fiscal-risk implications.

- **Status:** **ONGOING**; extension responds to continuing **West Asia** maritime logistics disruption.
- **RELIEF:** **Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation**; a time-bound intervention under the **Export Promotion Mission**.

# 2. Coverage
- **Component II:** Encourages exporters to obtain **ECGC** cover for eligible upcoming shipments to specified regions; provides **95% risk coverage** and limits premium increases for the eligible period.

- ⚠ **Trap:** Component II offers **95%**, not **100%**, risk coverage; **energy shipments are excluded**.

# 3. Exam focus
> Exam angle: **Programme / Initiative / Campaign**—test RELIEF’s expansion, launch date and Component II coverage.

national.headline: First two mineral blocks in Jammu and Kashmir auctioned through the Union mineral-auction process
facts: Two limestone blocks in Jammu and Kashmir were successfully auctioned through the Ministry of Mines’ Central Government mineral-auction process; the UT government entrusted the auction to the Ministry.
Koot–Kapran block is in Dooru tehsil, Anantnag district; it covers 22.43 hectares and has estimated resources of 4.75 million tonnes of limestone.
Wantrag block is in Anantnag district; it covers 5.36 hectares and has estimated resources of 10.853 million tonnes of limestone.
Koot–Kapran had been explored to G-4 stage; Wantrag had been explored to G-3 stage, including 159 metres of drilling.
The Ministry described the successful auction as a historic first for the UT; further exploration and development are still required.
national.summary: The auction marks Jammu and Kashmir’s first successful mineral-block auctions through the Central Government process. Both blocks are limestone deposits in Anantnag; the announcement concerns completed auctions, not completed mines or realised investment.
national.staticLink: Mineral-resource distribution, competitive allocation and sustainable mining under the MMDR framework.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The two auctioned limestone blocks are Koot–Kapran and Wantrag, both in Anantnag district, Jammu and Kashmir.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how transparent mineral auctions can support regional economic development, and why exploration, environmental safeguards and local participation remain essential.

national.headline: More than 2.42 lakh Special Gram Sabhas mark start of People’s Plan Campaign 2026–27
facts: More than 2.42 lakh Special Gram Sabhas were held across the country on Gandhi Jayanti, according to the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
The meetings marked the commencement of the People’s Plan Campaign 2026–27, ‘Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas’.
Panchayats will prepare Panchayat Development Plans for financial year 2027–28 under the campaign.
Discussions covered local priorities including water, sanitation, food security, land rights, livelihoods, women’s economic empowerment and Panchayat own-source revenue.
The Ministry said the Gram Sabha provided rural residents a platform to deliberate on government initiatives and locally relevant issues.
national.summary: The nationwide Special Gram Sabhas began the People’s Plan Campaign cycle for Panchayat Development Plans for 2027–28. The exercise centres participatory planning and local deliberation in rural governance.
national.staticLink: 73rd Constitutional Amendment, Gram Sabha and decentralised planning under Panchayati Raj.
national.prelimsTakeaway: ‘Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas’ is the People’s Plan Campaign 2026–27; the plans being prepared are for FY 2027–28.
national.mainsAngle: Evaluate how Gram Sabha deliberation can improve decentralised planning, accountability and inclusion, and identify capacity constraints that can limit participation.

national.headline: First tigress released in Buxa Tiger Reserve under tiger-reintroduction programme
facts: A tigress was released in Buxa Tiger Reserve, West Bengal, on 2 October 2026.
The release began a phased tiger-reintroduction programme intended to restore a viable, self-sustaining tiger population in the landscape.
The event was attended by the Union Environment Minister and the West Bengal Chief Minister.
The programme is framed around scientifically guided intervention and community participation.
Buxa Tiger Reserve is in West Bengal.
national.summary: The release initiated a phased tiger-reintroduction programme in Buxa Tiger Reserve. It is a conservation intervention; the release itself does not establish that a self-sustaining population has been restored.
national.staticLink: Project Tiger, tiger-reserve management and species reintroduction in fragmented landscapes.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Buxa Tiger Reserve is in West Bengal; a tigress was released there on 2 October 2026 to begin a phased reintroduction programme.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss the ecological and governance requirements for successful species reintroduction, including habitat connectivity, monitoring and community participation.

national.headline: Indian women’s hockey wins Asian Games gold; Sujeet and Indian boxers add gold medals
facts: India’s women’s hockey team won Asian Games gold, ending a wait of more than four decades, according to the Prime Minister’s Office release.
Sujeet won the men’s 65 kg freestyle wrestling gold; the Prime Minister’s Office described it as India’s first wrestling gold of this edition.
Lovlina Borgohain won the women’s 75 kg boxing gold with a 5–0 final victory.
Ankush won the men’s 80 kg boxing gold.

national.headline: Twenty-eight Ladakh places and features identified by standard names on Survey of India map
facts: The Union Government, in consultation with the Union Territory of Ladakh, identified 28 places and features for inclusion by standard names on the official Survey of India map.
The features include peaks, glaciers, passes, valleys, rivers, a lake and other land or water features.
Examples named in the release include Atisha Giri, Kanishka Peak, Skamri Glacier, Chapchingal Pass, Yangpa River and Guru Rinpoche Lake.
The stated purpose is more accurate recognition of the features and improved public awareness.

national.headline: Mumbai Port declares Jawahar Dweep Marine Oil Terminal plastic-free
facts: Mumbai Port Authority declared its Jawahar Dweep Marine Oil Terminal plastic-free on 2 October 2026.
The declaration was made during a Swachhata Abhiyan event at Mumbai Port.
The port authority said the status reflects efforts to reduce single-use plastic across port operations.
Oil-spill-response facilities were also dedicated to the nation at the event.
PIB described Jawahar Dweep as India’s first plastic-free oil terminal.
national.summary: Mumbai Port Authority declared Jawahar Dweep Marine Oil Terminal plastic-free as part of its waste-reduction efforts. The claim of a national first is reported by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways through PIB.

national.prelimsTakeaway: Jawahar Dweep Marine Oil Terminal is part of Mumbai Port; PIB identified it as India’s first plastic-free oil terminal.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how waste reduction and pollution-response measures can be integrated into port operations without compromising maritime and industrial activity.

# 2. Related event

national.headline: KVIC launches nationwide seasonal discounts on Khadi and village-industry products
facts: The Khadi and Village Industries Commission launched a nationwide discount campaign on 2 October 2026.
The campaign runs from 2 October to 16 November 2026.
The announced discount is up to 20% on Khadi products and 10% on village-industry products.
KVIC functions under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.
The release reported Khadi and village-industries sector turnover of more than ₹1.87 lakh crore in FY 2025–26 and employment for more than 2.04 crore people.
national.summary: KVIC launched a time-limited nationwide discount campaign for Khadi and village-industry goods, linking consumer promotion with support for artisans and weavers. The offer remains in effect until 16 November 2026.
national.staticLink: Khadi, village industries, rural livelihoods and the Swadeshi tradition.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The KVIC campaign offers up to 20% off Khadi and 10% off village-industry products from 2 October to 16 November 2026.
national.mainsAngle: Examine the role of Khadi and village industries in rural employment and local production, and assess the value and limits of discount-led demand promotion.

international.headline: Japan and the United States sign protocol indefinitely extending bilateral science-and-technology cooperation agreement
facts: Japan’s Foreign Minister Motegi Toshimitsu and U.S. science adviser Michael Kratsios signed the protocol in Tokyo on 2 October 2026.
The protocol indefinitely extends the bilateral agreement on cooperation in research and development in science and technology.
It amends provisions including the agreement’s annex on intellectual-property rights.
The two governments said the framework would support further cooperation, including on advanced technologies and AI in the Indo-Pacific and Global South.
international.summary: Japan and the United States signed a protocol to indefinitely extend their science-and-technology cooperation agreement and amend, among other provisions, its intellectual-property annex. The agreement provides a continuing framework for bilateral research cooperation; the announcement also highlighted advanced-technology and AI cooperation in the Indo-Pacific.

international.prelimsTakeaway: The protocol indefinitely extends the Japan–U.S. research-and-development cooperation agreement and amends its intellectual-property provisions.
international.mainsAngle: Assess how bilateral science agreements can shape technology standards, research partnerships and strategic cooperation in the Indo-Pacific.

- **Amendment:** Provisions including the agreement’s annex on intellectual-property rights

international.headline: WHO estimates show global life expectancy nearly recovered to its pre-pandemic level
facts: WHO released its latest Global Health Estimates on 2 October, covering health trends from 2000 to 2023.
Global life expectancy reached 73.3 years in 2023, close to 73.4 years in 2019.
Healthy life expectancy was 62.8 years in 2023, still 0.4 years below its 2019 level.
Non-communicable diseases accounted for 74% of global deaths in 2023, compared with 58% in 2000.
Eight of the ten leading causes of death worldwide in 2023 were non-communicable diseases.
international.summary: WHO’s 2026 Global Health Estimates indicate that average life expectancy had nearly returned to its pre-pandemic level by 2023, while healthy life expectancy remained lower. The estimates also show a growing share of deaths from non-communicable diseases, with implications for health-system priorities.
international.staticLink: Global burden of disease; life expectancy; epidemiological transition; non-communicable diseases
international.prelimsTakeaway: WHO reported global life expectancy of 73.3 years in 2023 versus 73.4 in 2019; NCDs accounted for 74% of deaths in 2023.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss the dual challenge for public health policy: recovering population health after a pandemic while preventing and managing the rising burden of chronic diseases.

sources.title: New WHO estimates show changing global health landscape
sources.publisher: World Health Organization

international.notes:
# 1. WHO estimates
- **Organisation:** **World Health Organization (WHO)**
- **Release / coverage:** **Global Health Estimates**, released **2 October 2026**; health trends from **2000 to 2023**
- **Status:** Released
# 2. Key indicators
| Indicator | Earlier benchmark | 2023 finding |
|---|---|---|
| Global life expectancy | **73.4 years (2019)** | **73.3 years** |
| Healthy life expectancy | **2019 level: 0.4 years above 2023** | **62.8 years** |
| NCD share of global deaths | **58% (2000)** | **74%** |
- **Leading causes:** **8 of the 10** leading causes of death worldwide in **2023** were non-communicable diseases (**NCDs**).
- ⚠ **Trap:** Life expectancy had nearly returned to its **2019** level; healthy life expectancy was still **0.4 years** below its **2019** level.
> Exam angle: Report — distinguish life expectancy from healthy life expectancy and note the rising share of deaths from NCDs.

international.headline: PAHO members approve regional strategies on health emergencies, antimicrobial resistance and arboviral diseases
facts: The 63rd PAHO Directing Council concluded in Washington, D.C., on 2 October 2026.
Member States approved a health-emergency and risk-management strategy for 2026–2031 and an antimicrobial-resistance action plan for 2027–2031.
The Council also approved an integrated strategy for prevention and control of arboviral diseases for 2026–2035, including dengue, chikungunya and Zika.
PAHO reported that the Americas recorded more than 13 million dengue cases and over 8,400 deaths in 2024.
A regional food-safety strategy for 2026–2031 was also approved.
international.summary: At its 63rd Directing Council, PAHO members adopted regional strategies covering health-emergency preparedness, antimicrobial resistance, arboviral diseases and food safety. The decisions set multi-year priorities for regional cooperation and health-system resilience in the Americas.
international.staticLink: International health governance; One Health; epidemic preparedness; antimicrobial resistance
international.prelimsTakeaway: The PAHO Directing Council concluded on 2 October 2026; approved plans include AMR action for 2027–2031 and arboviral-disease control for 2026–2035.
international.mainsAngle: Examine how regional health institutions can strengthen preparedness, surveillance and coordinated responses to cross-border health threats.

international.headline: WFP warns of worsening food insecurity in Yemen as conflict displaces families
facts: WFP reported on 2 October that more than 149,000 people had been displaced by renewed fighting, citing the International Organization for Migration.
WFP monitoring in accessible areas found that 74% of households could not meet basic food needs, a reported high for 2026.
WFP said 18.3 million people in Yemen faced acute food insecurity and 2.2 million children under five were acutely malnourished.
Yemen imports around 90% of its food, leaving supply and prices exposed to disruption in trade routes and markets.
WFP had assisted more than 70,000 people in displacement hotspots and said it might need to scale emergency assistance to 1.5 million people.
international.summary: Previous: coverage focused on the UN envoy, Houthi talks and Red Sea escalation. Today: WFP issued a new warning that conflict-related displacement, market disruption and restricted humanitarian access are worsening food insecurity, and outlined its response plans.
international.staticLink: Conflict-driven food insecurity; humanitarian assistance; food-supply vulnerability; Bab al-Mandab maritime corridor
international.prelimsTakeaway: WFP’s 2 October warning cited 18.3 million people facing acute food insecurity in Yemen and 74% of monitored households unable to meet basic food needs.
international.mainsAngle: Analyse how conflict and disruption to strategic shipping corridors can compound food insecurity, displacement and humanitarian-access challenges.

- ⚠ **Trap:** More than **70,000 people** had received assistance; assistance to **1.5 million** was a potential scale-up, not a completed response.
> Exam angle: Report — distinguish monitored household food needs, acute food insecurity and WFP’s completed versus possible assistance.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the WHO estimates reported on 2 October 2026?
options: Global life expectancy reached 73.3 years in 2023, while healthy life expectancy was 62.8 years.
Global life expectancy reached 62.8 years in 2023, while healthy life expectancy was 73.3 years.
Non-communicable diseases accounted for 58% of global deaths in 2023.
Only five of the ten leading causes of death worldwide in 2023 were non-communicable diseases.
mcqs.explanation: WHO reported life expectancy of 73.3 years and healthy life expectancy of 62.8 years in 2023. Non-communicable diseases accounted for 74% of deaths.

mcqs.question: Which statement about the Andhra Pradesh High Court’s ruling on local-body reservations is correct?
options: It upheld both state orders and found that no empirical exercise was required.
It set aside the orders exceeding the 50% aggregate ceiling without the required empirical exercise, while leaving open reconsideration after such an exercise.
It ruled that BC reservation in local bodies was permanently prohibited.
It directed local-body elections to be postponed indefinitely.
mcqs.explanation: The Court set aside the enhanced reservation orders, citing the aggregate ceiling and missing empirical exercise, and directed the election process to begin expeditiously.

mcqs.question: Which statement accurately describes the Global Horticulture Hub–Rayalaseema Rising plan?
options: Its target is to increase horticulture area from 8.41 lakh hectares to 14.41 lakh hectares across 10 districts.
It has already expanded horticulture area to 14.41 lakh hectares in all 10 districts.
It is limited to 10 mandals and 201 villages.
Its entire estimated outlay is government investment, with no private investment expected.
mcqs.explanation: The plan targets expansion from 8.41 lakh to 14.41 lakh hectares across 10 districts. Its estimated outlay includes government investment and expected private investment; the target is not a completed expansion.

mcqs.question: Which statement about the proposed compressed-biogas investment plan announced for Andhra Pradesh is correct?
options: The ₹1 lakh-crore investment has been fully spent and the plants are operational.
The announcement is a proposed investment plan; the projected jobs and state revenue are not realised outcomes.
District-wise plant locations and a construction schedule were specified in the announcement.
The plan was announced by the Ministry of Mines as part of the Jammu and Kashmir auction process.
mcqs.explanation: The reported ₹1 lakh-crore plan and projected jobs and revenue are announcements and projections, not evidence of completed investment or operational plants.

mcqs.question: Which set of PAHO measures was approved by its 63rd Directing Council?
options: Strategies on health emergencies, antimicrobial resistance, arboviral diseases, and food safety

A global treaty on Khadi products and village industries
A plan to establish an agricultural school in Andhra Pradesh
